title: The AI boom is making the world’s cheapest smartphones disappear
key_facts: Prices of existing smartphone models have risen about 15% globally this year and newly launched models are about 25% dearer than last year, as a global memory chip shortage driven by AI data centre demand pushes up manufacturing costs.
Increases vary by region: 21% in India, 19% across Asia-Pacific, 18% in the Middle East and Africa and 5% in the US.
Chinese makers, which ship about 60% of the world's smartphones, have 'drastically reduced' entry-level projects and favour premium phones, Counterpoint analyst Ivan Lam told Rest of World.

Shipments of phones under $100 fell almost 60% year on year in the second quarter of 2026 (IDC); 173 million shipped last year; in Africa they fell 34% in the quarter and Oppo's sub-$100 shipments in Southeast Asia fell 96% (Omdia).
Xiaomi raised the price of a 128GB Redmi 15C in India from 12,499 rupees ($140) in December to 16,999 rupees ($190) in June, up 36%.

IDC's Ramon Llamas says the three main memory makers (Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron, more than 90% of the market) pivoted most supply to AI data centres in late 2025 and the shortage is unlikely to ease soon.

GSMA foundation's Claire Sibthorpe warns that unaffordable phones could widen the digital divide; an entry-level device costs the poorest 20% the equivalent of 44% of monthly income, and 76% in sub-Saharan Africa (GSMA September report).
S&P Global estimates US hyperscalers' capital spending at $870 billion in 2026, rising above $1.3 trillion in 2027.
quote_evidence: The world’s cheapest smartphones are disappearing because AI infrastructure is absorbing the components.
Prices of existing smartphone models have risen by about 15% globally this year, while newly launched models are roughly 25% more expensive than last year.
The 173 million sub-$100 smartphones shipped globally last year are disappearing, with shipments falling almost 60% year over year in the second quarter of 2026, according to IDC.
why_it_matters_hint: Dearer and scarcer budget phones could keep lower-income people in poorer regions offline.
event_date: Published 5 Oct 2026; data to the second quarter of 2026.
notes: Read in full. Figures come from IDC, Counterpoint, Omdia, GSMA and S&P Global as Rest of World quotes them; the causal link to AI data centre demand rests on analysts' assessments. Url is the clean link (no utm codes), as fixed in url_fixes.json.
